mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand with sectoral rotation into housing, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as housing-related equities outperform.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
regime_hint: late-cycle demand slowdown with housing strength
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically greater than the market median in periods matching the trigger condition (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) drop below 4.5% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth remains flat signals labor market tightness without wage inflation, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to improved corporate margins.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to lower earnings expectations in industrial sectors.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for four consecutive months while FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which historically coincides with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 102 for four consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS > 4.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically above the market median in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 5% while personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) grow below 1% signals a shift from spending to saving, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to lower retail demand.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly growth > 5% AND GDPC1 monthly growth < 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals a weak labor market, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate hiring constraints.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.7% for two consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate earnings in industrial sectors.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.7% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).
